claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing/full fiscal-year 2026 revenue, the first time, per Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 results.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion (up from $106 billion a year earlier) as of Q2 2026.
AWS's AI business and its chips business (custom Trainium and Graviton silicon) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Gartner forecast that by 2028 cloud-native platforms will be the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
AWS reported $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.

Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year; remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363%; prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals total $75 billion.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers found 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Gartner predicted that by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said developers are standardizing on CNCF projects and organizations are extending platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree AI agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months; 63% say they trust agents to make production changes; teams expecting agents to generate half or more of infrastructure code rise from 45% to 52% within six months.
Pulumi's report describes the trust-versus-manual-approval gap as stated trust outrunning real guardrails, and says manual approval remains close to universal today.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence says the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%, with 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to maturity.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit, and Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server for Kubernetes.
Pulumi Agent Skills teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects.
Hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030 per ResearchAndMarkets.
Gartner predicts 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds per Mordor Intelligence.
The 2026 predictions held up; last year's edition predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
